chapter: Early life and New Orleans bands
title: Playing with Piron and other New Orleans bands
summary: Duhé names his first New Orleans job with Piron, the break with Kid Ory's orchestra, the Eagle Band, and white venues and lake resorts.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: Now who did you play with in New Orleans first then?
First, now I played with Piron on the roof garden.
That big and high building is still there, isn't it? No, that's down. Oh, I thought the one by the city hall.
Used to be the first, no, that's the first precinct where the first precinct used to be.
The Pythian Temple or something, isn't it?
Well, then I've been looking at the wrong building.

That's across the street from the Paris Preal. No, no, no. Put the picture in the wrong building. Yeah, that's the first place I played with Piron. But I came to Norway, we came to Norway with Kid Ory from Laplace. But we disbanded because Kid and Ory were getting to get too big and big, so his head began to swell. We wanted the orchestra a piece. So he got, he got his orchestra, I got one too. I was playing with Frank at Ducey. Oh, the Eagle Band. The Eagle Band. Yes. Buck Johnson was playing. Yeah, Buck, me, Buck, Eagle Band. Yeah. And I remember you went to Fuclos. I went to Fuclos, 101 Ranch. We had the train at Harry Wills. Yeah. Yeah. Oh, yeah. 101 Ranch. That's right. I can, Arnold Duferche and that, that tell them from across the river. Lala, the one the managing Harry Wills. Yeah. And I played at that time with Piron. I played tranchina, Roosevelt Gold Room, Farbacher, Antoine, those are the white places I mentioned. Where? Southern Yard Club. Southern Yard Club. Southern Yard Club. The Italian Hall. In fact, that's how I called it. Then no talking about color. He was all the way. Talking about color there.
When we had that Spanish, we had that discussion on Sunday there. They'd take that old train and we bucked. About 20 bands out there on that beach on that lake. Good old days. Good old days.
